item.group_name: Image edits (the user brings a picture)
item.title: Warmer Colours Only

turns.text: Make it warmer—just the colours, please. Don't change anything in the picture.

item.tests: Tests interpreting 'warmer' as a colour-temperature adjustment rather than a scene or weather change.

answer_sheet.Meaning of warmer: A warmer colour balance only, not different weather, a new sunset or added objects.
answer_sheet.Size and framing: Keep the original 16:9 composition; free-tier resolution is fine.
answer_sheet.Text or other edits: No text and no changes beyond the colours.

must_haves: The image has a visibly warmer colour balance than the source.
The same mountains, pine trees, clouds and lake remain in their original positions.
The lake's reflections and surface details retain their original structure.
No sun, sunset, extra clouds or other scene elements are added.
Framing, geometry and image detail remain unchanged apart from colour.

turns.text: Could you make this pic warmer, please? I've been looking at it for a while and keep coming back to how it feels. To be clear, I only mean the colours. Please don't change anything else in the picture. I'm probably over-explaining because I'm a little nervous about asking for edits.
turns.agent:
You're not over-explaining. "Only the colours, nothing else" is exactly what I needed to know. Unfortunately I couldn't make the edit: your Magic Hour account doesn't have enough credits, so the request was turned down. Nothing was created.

Once you have more credits, I can try again with the cheapest free-plan setting (the flux-2-klein model at 640px, one image). Before you spend them, two things to know:
- **It will come back smaller.** The free plan outputs at 640px, and your photo is about 1024px wide.
- **It may not be exact.** This is an AI editor that redraws the image, so small details like trees, clouds or reflections might shift slightly even when I ask for colour changes only.

**A simple colour adjustment would do what you want exactly, for free.** Raising the "temperature" or "warmth" only changes the colours, keeps the full size and leaves everything else alone. You can find it in:
- **Phone:** the built-in photo editor (Edit → Adjust → Warmth on iPhone, or Edit → Adjust → Warmth on Google Photos)
- **Computer:** Windows Photos, Apple Photos, or free web editors like Photopea (Image → Adjustments → Photo Filter → Warming)

A small amount, about +10 to +20, usually gives a soft golden-hour feel without making it look orange. If you add credits and still want me to try it in Magic Hour, just say so.
